chunks: Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn al-Muhtadī, who said:
I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام and said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, my brother died, and I married his wife.”
Then my uncle came and claimed that he had secretly married her. So I asked her about that, and she denied it most strongly, saying: “There was never anything at all between me and him.”
So he عليه السلام said: “Her acknowledgment is binding upon you, and her denial is binding upon him.”

key_terms.أَنْكَرَتْ: she denied; the woman’s categorical rejection of the claim
key_terms.إِقْرَارُهَا: her acknowledgment; her statement as legally binding evidence
key_terms.إِنْكَارُهَا: her denial; her rejection of the claim as binding against the claimant
key_terms.ادَّعَى: he claimed; indicates a legal assertion requiring consideration
key_terms.امْرَأَتَهُ: his wife; the widow at the center of the legal dispute
key_terms.تَزَوَّجْتُ: I married; refers to the speaker’s marriage to his deceased brother’s wife
key_terms.سِرًّا: secretly; describing the alleged hidden marriage
key_terms.عَمِّي: my paternal uncle; the one making the claim of prior secret marriage

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام rule in a dispute over an alleged secret marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal dispute concerning a claimed secret marriage after a widow remarried. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام rules that the woman’s statement is authoritative in relation to both parties: her confirmation establishes matters for the husband, and her denial stands against the claimant. The narration highlights evidentiary weight in family and marriage law.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4650 - Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi who said:
I asked Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as): "May I be sacrificed for you!
My brother passed away, and I married his wife.

Then my uncle came and claimed that he had secretly married her.
I asked her about this, and she strongly denied it, saying, 'There was never anything between me and him at all.'"
Imam (as) replied: "Her acknowledgment is binding upon you, and her denial is binding upon him."
